title: Crewship panel payload — embed.v1
description: The one escape hatch (PRD §3.1): a cross-origin sandboxed iframe showing a page a HUMAN OPERATOR has already vetted. The payload names which of the vetted sources to show — it does not carry a URL, and there is no field one could travel in. The server resolves the name against the instance's embed allow-list and attaches the resolved URL on the way out; a producer that is not in the allow-list's vocabulary cannot make a browser fetch anything.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference (informational; the server ignores it). Present so a hand-written payload gets inline validation in an editor while a producer script is being developed.

source.description: The NAME of one entry in the instance's embed allow-list — `grafana-fleet`, `status-page`. Not a URL, and deliberately not a URL: an iframe src is fetched by the READER's browser, from the reader's network, at render time, so a URL a producer could change on every push would be a covert channel out of the workspace exactly like the image tag §8 rule 2 removes and the rendered link §8 rule 3 removes. This is §8 rule 4's shape applied to embeds — the human declares the allow-list, the machine selects from it — and a name from a closed set leaks log2(n) bits per push instead of an arbitrary payload. An unknown name is refused; it is never fetched to find out.

caption.description: One line of plain text drawn by host chrome above the frame ("eu-west · since the 12:40 incident"), so a reader can tell why THIS source is showing. Plain text: no markup, no URL, no entity reference. It renders through the React element renderer like every other panel string (§8 rule 10).

$comment: The absences are the specification, not an oversight, and each one is a field some other product shipped and regretted. No `url`/`src` — see `source` above. No `html`, `srcdoc` or `markup`: §8 rule 1 says the agent fills a schema and never emits markup, and Grafana's Angular HTML panel is the named prior art for why (killed in v10; the community rebuilt it unsupervised). No `sandbox`, `allow` or `csp`: the host owns the sandbox, and a payload that could widen it is a payload that can remove it — `allow-scripts allow-same-origin` together let a frame delete its own sandbox attribute. No `width`/`height`: producer-controlled geometry is a panel that can cover the page it sits on, and §3.1 pins sizing as negotiated rather than free. No `image`: §8 rule 2, absent rather than sanitised.
